findings.finding: The native focus retains the source's photographic grain and tonal staining, but introduces red-brown islands and pale colour boundaries along the upper facade strip between windows. Some coincide with source staining; others imply a distinct exposed substrate or chipped coating that cannot be resolved from the supplied grayscale source. I cannot certify that these are only hue variations on the existing surface, nor establish a definite geometric alteration. Human material-boundary review is required rather than a positive vote.

All four upper windows, three lower windows, entrance, basement openings, steps, moldings, chimneys, wiring, archive marks, dog, drain/tray, pavement and litter remain aligned. White archive border is retained.
Faint door marks and tiny plaques retain source-level shapes and legibility; no exact house-number reading is asserted.
Ordinary brown/ochre/roof-red choices remain allowed provisional hypotheses. The review concerns local material segmentation, not the absence of historically proven colour.

Matched dimensions and very close grayscale structure support the visual preservation findings but are not a visual pass or proof of historical colours. Chroma-only material patterns must be judged in colour.

data.method: Pillow grayscale BT601 coefficients on stored nonlinear RGB; no geometric registration or source/output changes. Comparison is diagnostic, not a visual verdict.
